liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (3 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Easy Wind among the very best versions, a top-five performance; Reviewer considers this a top Easy Wind and a classic American song [9][10][11]
- **Dark Star** (1 review, 1 other source): Dark Star begins with a rough splice, runs 17:22, and passes through many phases; Easy Wind flows continuously into Dark Star here, suggesting the Yellow Dog Story on the other source may be from another date [4][14]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Opening lacks the power of later versions, apparently from technical or sound problems, but it turns into a classic version [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **lead in**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-09-01.157433.sbd.grner1.goody.1644** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 123 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1969-09-01.sbd.kaplan.5216.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1969-09-01.171656.BatonRougeLA.sbd.anon.gems.flac1644**: soundboard; 10 songs; 93 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: A splice leaves a brief gap after Dark Star's beginning, and Lovelight has a few seconds of tape damage [3]
- **gd69-09-01.sbd.vernon.19963.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 94 min; rated 3.93/5 by 15 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says TC's organ adds a pleasant ambience to the music [6]

## Around the show

- Almanac reportedly shows the temperature reached 89 degrees that day, perhaps explaining the loose, strange feel of the show [11]
- Drunks near the front kept shouting for White Rabbit during the Airplane's set and into the Dead's set [12]
- Jerry said it wasn't their song; Bob suggested listening to the record at home; audience members threw things at hecklers [12]
- Reviewer places the show at the first New Orleans Pop Festival, held at a racetrack near Baton Rouge [17]
- Notes describe this as the band's first rock festival, at a race track in Prairieville, Louisiana [3]
- Reviewer calls this possibly the second-best version, looser than 9/20/70 because Bobby's playing improved dramatically in between [11]
- Unlike the previous circulating copy, Casey Jones is not clipped and this tape lacks the Yellow Dog Story before Dark Star [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-09-01.157433.sbd.grner1.goody.1644**: transferred by Remaster by grner1, goody; source: Source 1 (unedited): cassette master > ? > CD's received in trade. Source 2 (edited): MSC (Ampex C-90 cassette) > DAT > CD-R (via Andy Lemieux and Kingbee). [1]. Also: About 14 minutes at the end of Lovelight is spliced in from the edited, known-lineage Source 2 because the unedited source was cut; A seamless splice removed a few seconds; the original spliced, properly tuned version is included in a bonus folder [1]
- **gd1969-09-01.sbd.kaplan.5216.shnf**: transferred by (Extraction and.shn encoding by Seth Kaplan via EAC and MKW.; source: SBD>Cm>Dat>CD [2]. Also: Kaplan's version adds a William Tell track and breaks the St. Stephen to The Eleven continuity heard on Live/Dead [16]
- **gd1969-09-01.171656.BatonRougeLA.sbd.anon.gems.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Augustus Owsley Stanley III (aka Bear); transferred by Mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Bear's Ampex Cassette Master > DAT > CD > WAV (provided by Anon) [3]. Also: Aired on KXCI Tucson's Dead Air on September 1, 2024, hosted by Jim Blackwood, then shared to shnflac.net in June 2025 [3]
- **gd69-09-01.sbd.vernon.19963.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux, Kingbee, Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: This soundboard is an upgrade over earlier copies, and its text file raises a puzzle about the Yellow Dog story; Transcribers cut the between-song stage banter from this circulating version [6][12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead Performances At Race Tracks 1969-88](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2013/07/grateful-dead-performances-at-race.html) [25]
